description: The DIAMOND trial (DIaMonD) tested whether continuous glucose monitoring improves HbA1c in adults with T1DM on multiple daily injections. The original trial enrolled adults with HbA1c ≥ 7.5%. CGM-based pre-screening identifies patients with suboptimal glucose control who are most likely to benefit. This protocol targets T1DM patients specifically — T2DM patients should be screened against the GLP-1 T2DM protocol instead.

inclusion_criteria.human_rationale: The DIAMOND trial was specifically designed for T1DM patients on multiple daily injections. T2DM patients have different pathophysiology and respond differently to CGM intervention — they are excluded by design to ensure the study population is homogeneous.

The DIAMOND trial required HbA1c ≥ 7.5% at enrolment. GMI (computed from mean CGM glucose) is the CGM-native equivalent. Patients below this threshold are already well-controlled and less likely to show meaningful improvement from CGM therapy.

Patients with GMI above 10% (estimated HbA1c > 10%) may have acute complications or non-compliance issues requiring medical stabilisation before trial enrolment. An upper cap is standard across CGM trials.

ADA 2024 defines ≥ 70% TIR as adequate control for T1DM. Patients already achieving ≥ 70% TIR are not the target population for a CGM intervention study — the trial recruits patients who stand to benefit most.

exclusion_criteria.human_rationale: More than one severe hypoglycaemic event (< 54 mg/dL) in the monitoring period indicates a high-risk safety profile. These patients require immediate clinical review rather than trial enrolment. This mirrors the DIAMOND trial's safety exclusion criteria.

notes: v2: Added diabetes_type == T1DM inclusion criterion. Based on Beck RW et al., Effect of Continuous Glucose Monitoring on Glycemic Control in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes Using Insulin Injections, JAMA 2017;317(4):371–378.
